hypothesis.statement: The multiset residual `target-only: +1 mr / ours-only: -1 li` is the LIVE-ZERO COPY-vs-REMAT class, and this function is unusually strong evidence that the class is genuinely allocator-side rather than merely unprobed: the source ALREADY SPELLS THE COPY EXPLICITLY and MWCC still rematerialises. At +0x68-0x7c the target emits `li r7,0 / stw r7,32(r4) / mr r4,r7 / li r5,-1` -- one zero materialised and then COPIED -- where ours emits `li r0,0 / stw r0,32(r3) / li r8,0 / li r6,0 / ... / li r3,-1`, three separate zeros. The `mr r4,r7` corresponds to the existing source statement `moveOffset = j;`, which is already a written-out copy of a variable known to be zero. A next lane should therefore NOT spend probes re-spelling that assignment; the open question is whether the two zero webs (`j` and `moveOffset`) can be made to interfere so the allocator cannot afford two registers.
